agent.problem: The question refers to "the city" without identifying it as Jerusalem. Understanding which city was breached depends on earlier cards that are no longer on screen.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

agent.problem: "The walls are open" retells the breach from Jeremiah 39:2, but the card cites only Jeremiah 39:3. The citation is too narrow for everything the card tells.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

agent.problem: "And so are all the nobles of Judah" implies that the nobles were also killed before Zedekiah's eyes. Verse 6 says that Zedekiah's sons were slaughtered before his eyes, but separately says that the nobles were killed; it does not clearly imply that he watched the nobles die.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

agent.problem: "They" has no antecedent within the question. Knowing that it means Nebuzaradan and the Babylonian officials depends on story card 10, which is no longer on screen.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

agent.problem: Gedaliah has not appeared or been hinted at in the earlier cards, and his lineage gives the baker no way to reason out his name. The blank therefore asks for unseen wording from verse 14 rather than a meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
